The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. This means that the rhombus can be divided into four congruent right-angled triangles.

$16 = \frac{d_2}{2}$

$$E_p(n!) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \left\lfloor \frac{n}{p^k} \right\rfloor$$

$\left\lfloor \frac{200}{81} \right\rfloor = \lfloor 2.46... \rfloor = 2$
